topics.titleTr: AI'nin Yazdigi PR'lari Incelemek: Insan Kontrol Listesi
topics.titleEn: Reviewing AI-Generated Pull Requests: A Checklist
topics.angle: checklist|Give reviewers a checklist for safely merging code written by AI agents.
topics.brief: Sections: why AI-authored PRs need a different review lens (plausible-but-wrong code, silent scope creep, hidden dependencies, fabricated tests, license/security risks); a concrete review checklist (verify the diff does what the description says, run the tests, check edge cases and error paths, scan new deps, look for deleted safeguards); how to keep humans accountable as AI writes more code; team norms and CI gates. Key claims to verify: common AI-code failure modes; the rise of AI-authored PRs. Sources: engineering blogs on AI code review, 2026 reports on AI in R&D. Contrarian: 'the AI wrote it' is not a reason to trust it.

topics.titleTr: Geri Basinc ve Yuk Atma: Servisi Ayakta Tutmak
topics.titleEn: Backpressure and Load Shedding: Survive Overload
topics.angle: deep-dive|Explain how services stay alive under overload with backpressure and load shedding.
topics.brief: Sections: what happens when demand exceeds capacity (queues grow, latency explodes, cascading failure); backpressure (signal upstream to slow down, bounded queues, flow control); load shedding (drop or degrade low-priority work, admission control, prioritization); patterns (token buckets at the edge, deadlines/timeouts, brownout mode); observability signals to watch. Key claims to verify: mechanics of bounded queues, deadline propagation, admission control. Sources: SRE/queueing-theory references and resilience engineering writeups. Distinct from existing rate-limiting and retries/circuit-breaker briefs: focus on overload survival. Story-led: an outage that shedding would have prevented.

topics.titleTr: Web Speech API: Web Uygulamasina Sesli Giris Ekle
topics.titleEn: Web Speech API: Add Voice Input to Your App
topics.angle: how-to|Show how to add speech recognition and synthesis to a web app with sensible fallbacks.
topics.brief: Sections: why voice-first UX is rising in 2026 web apps; the Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition and SpeechSynthesis) and browser support/quirks; a working example (voice search/dictation with interim results); handling permissions, languages, and errors; accessibility wins and pitfalls; when to fall back to a server-side STT API. Key claims to verify: current browser support and API behavior; privacy/permission model. Sources: MDN Web Speech API docs, 2026 frontend trend reports. Field-notes: what breaks across browsers and how to degrade gracefully.

topics.titleEn: CSS Cascade Layers: Tame Big Stylesheets with @layer
topics.angle: how-to|Teach @layer to control specificity and integrate third-party CSS cleanly.
topics.brief: Sections: the specificity problem @layer solves (utility vs component vs override wars, !important creep); how cascade layers work (layer order beats specificity); a practical setup (reset, third-party, components, utilities, overrides); integrating frameworks and design systems; interaction with :where(), imports, and unlayered styles; migration tips. Key claims to verify: @layer ordering rules and browser support in 2026; interaction with specificity. Sources: MDN @layer docs, modern-CSS writeups. Distinct from existing :has()/nesting brief. Story-led: refactoring a tangled stylesheet with layers.

topics.titleTr: Uctan Uca Tip Guvenli API'ler: tRPC ve Otesi
topics.titleEn: End-to-End Type-Safe APIs: tRPC and Beyond
topics.keywordEn: end to end type safe api trpc
topics.angle: comparison|Compare approaches to sharing types between server and client without a codegen mess.
topics.brief: Sections: what end-to-end type safety buys you (refactors that don't break the client, no drift between server and UI); approaches compared (tRPC, typed OpenAPI + codegen, GraphQL + codegen, framework server actions, schema-first with Zod); tradeoffs (monorepo coupling vs public APIs, boundaries, versioning); when each fits; a starter recipe. Key claims to verify: current capabilities of tRPC and typed-OpenAPI tooling in 2026. Sources: tRPC and OpenAPI-typescript docs, framework guides. Distinct from existing REST-vs-GraphQL and RHF+Zod briefs: focus on cross-boundary type sharing.

topics.titleTr: Tukenmeden Cok Platformda Yayin: Bir Dagitim Sistemi
topics.titleEn: Cross-Post Without Burning Out: A Multi-Platform System
topics.angle: how-to|Build a repeatable system to publish one idea across 3-5 platforms without doubling the work.
topics.brief: Sections: why 2026 creators grow fastest posting to 3-5 platforms; the reformat-not-repost rule (adapt hook, aspect ratio, captions, length per platform); a weekly system (one shoot -> master edit -> platform-specific cuts -> schedule); tooling and templates; measuring which platform earns the effort; avoiding shadow-ban and duplicate-content traps. Key claims to verify: the 3-5 platform growth finding; platform reformatting norms and length limits. Sources: Sprout Social/Sendible 2026 social trend reports, creator playbooks. Distinct from the 'where to post' and 'batch a month' briefs: this is the distribution workflow. Field-notes: one week's real pipeline.

topics.titleTr: Kisa Video Ne Kadar Uzun Olmali? 2026 Verileri
topics.titleEn: How Long Should a Short Video Be in 2026?
topics.angle: guide|Use current data to pick the right length per platform instead of defaulting to 15 seconds.
topics.brief: Sections: the 2026 shift (60-90s clips often outperform 15s on most platforms); platform length limits and sweet spots (TikTok, Reels up to ~20 min, Shorts up to ~3 min); why longer-but-valuable beats ultra-short (watch time, completion, saves); how length interacts with hook and retention; a decision guide by content type. Key claims to verify: the 60-90s outperformance claim; current platform length caps. Sources: OpusClip/Sprout Social 2026 short-form trend reports. Data-led: lead with retention/length data. Distinct from existing hook/retention briefs: the question here is duration.

topics.titleTr: Ciz ve Paylas: Yaraticilar Icin ChatGPT Sketch
topics.titleEn: Draw It, Post It: ChatGPT Sketch for Creators
topics.angle: how-to|Show creators how to turn rough sketches into on-brand social graphics with ChatGPT Images 2.5.
topics.brief: Sections: what ChatGPT Images 2.5 Sketch is (draw a rough layout, @Sketch or the + menu, convert to a finished image, iterate); a reusable canvas workflow for thumbnails, carousels and post graphics; keeping outputs on-brand (reference style, palette, text handling); speed gains vs prompt-only generation; limits and where a real designer still wins; disclosure/authenticity notes. Key claims to verify: how @Sketch works and where it's available; Images 2.5 release Sept 8 2026 and speed improvements. Sources: OpenAI Images 2.5 announcement, hands-on reviews (TechRadar). Distinct from the broad 'AI social graphics' brief: this is the specific Sketch workflow.

topics.titleEn: Analyze Data on Your Phone with Gemini in Sheets
topics.angle: how-to|Show how to summarize data and build charts from your phone with Gemini in Google Sheets.
topics.brief: Sections: what shipped (Gemini in Google Sheets on Android, rollout from Sept 9 2026); how to use it (open a sheet, tap Ask Gemini/the spark icon, prompts like 'Summarize this table' and 'Analyze for insights', generate charts on-device); real field use cases (checking numbers on the go, quick insights, outlier flags); the mobile limits (complex edits, formulas and formatting still need the web); privacy and data notes. Key claims to verify: Android availability and rollout date, supported vs unsupported actions on mobile. Sources: Google Workspace Updates blog, Ubergizmo coverage Sept 2026. Field-notes: what actually works on a phone.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT'de Is ve Kisisel Hesaplari Birlikte Kullan
topics.titleEn: Connect Work and Personal Accounts in ChatGPT
topics.angle: how-to|Show how to connect multiple accounts to ChatGPT plugins without mixing work and personal data.
topics.brief: Sections: what changed (ChatGPT now supports multiple accounts per plugin, beyond just Gmail/Calendar/Contacts, so personal and work accounts coexist in one chat); how to connect and switch accounts safely; a workflow that keeps work and personal data separated (naming, default account, scoping requests); the permission model and low-risk-action defaults to review; pitfalls (accidental cross-account actions, data leakage) and how to audit connections. Key claims to verify: multi-account plugin support and the plugin-permissions default behavior. Sources: OpenAI ChatGPT release notes Sept 2026. How-to: concrete setup plus a safety pass.
